description:
**The load-bearing fixture.** Six observations instead of two, all of them shared, none of them separating.

A criterion that quietly tracks evidence *volume* rather than whether evidence separates passes `symmetric_rivals` and passes `discriminating` and fails only here. There is no other fixture in the set that could tell, which is why this one decides whether the result means anything.

Direct descendant of experiment 2's `near_miss` (same topic, near-identical wording, no edges, so zero movement) and experiment 4's `distractor_web`. Both existed because a mechanism that looks right on a two-node web is not yet known to be reading the graph.

Also a guard against a second confound: `stake_of` averages evidence salience rather than summing it, so one record and six produce identical stake. The dissonance channel is therefore blind to the difference between this fixture and `symmetric_rivals` by construction - which is exactly why the criterion must not be built on that channel. Requirements section 12.

expect.note: Structural. Three times the evidence of `symmetric_rivals` with the same separation structure - which is to say, none. Pre-registration section 3 predicts the meta-belief lands within 0.05 of its `symmetric_rivals` value, and states in advance why the criterion cannot see the difference.

evidence.summary: The distant supernovae are dimmer than a static model predicts.
The dimming is the same in every direction we have measured.
The scatter in supernova magnitudes is consistent across the sample.
The distance ladder calibration has been checked against two independent anchors.
The survey reaches the same depth in each observed field.
Extinction by intervening dust has been bounded and is too small to account for the effect.

beliefs.proposition: The dimming is best explained by a change in expansion over time.
The dimming is best explained by our position within a large underdense region.
